narrative: The model estimates about a one-in-five chance (19%) that you will not pass your final year; it is not a certainty, but under the school’s rule this risk is enough to require remedial courses. The strongest warning sign was your intention not to continue into higher education. In the comparison group of students who passed, every student wanted to go on to higher education, so your answer was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward failing. The second most important factor was why you chose this school: choosing it for its reputation worked in your favor and pushed toward passing, although among passers course choice was more common than reputation. The third was your record of past class failures. You have none, matching the average for passers, so this also pushed toward passing. Even with those two favorable factors, the first factor was strong enough that the overall profile was flagged for support. Next, speak with your counsellor about the remedial plan, set a realistic path toward continuing education if that is your goal, and protect against future failure by attending more consistently—your 12 absences are well above the passers’ average of about four—and by increasing study time and using family support.
